result: Sst-IN→PC connections emerge at P7-8, with connection probability increasing significantly from P7-8 to P9-11 and remaining stable from P9 to P20. Coinciding with eye opening, there is a ~65% reduction in uIPSC amplitude from P12-13 to P14-15.
evaluation: Claims C30-C34 provide comprehensive developmental data showing emergence, maturation, and weakening of Sst-IN→PC connections. The temporal correlation with eye opening (C34) is supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2 showing eye opening timing. Statistical analyses (χ² test, one-way ANOVA) support the quantitative claims.

result: The weakening of Sst-IN→PC synaptic transmission during eye opening occurs not only in visual cortex but also in the prefrontal Cg1/2 area, with similar ~65% reduction in uIPSC amplitude from P12-13 to P14-15.
evaluation: Claims C40-C42 demonstrate that the eye opening-dependent weakening of Sst-IN→PC transmission is not restricted to visual cortex. Statistical analysis (one-way ANOVA, p=6.0×10⁻⁴) supports the amplitude reduction. This extends the main finding beyond sensory cortex.

result: FS-IN→PC synaptic transmission increases during eye opening, with ~140% increase in uIPSC amplitude from P12-13 to P14-15, while connection probability remains stable. The 10-90% rise time becomes significantly shorter at P16-18.
evaluation: Claims C43-C48 provide comprehensive characterization of FS-IN→PC development. The increase in synaptic strength (one-way ANOVA, p=4.6×10⁻⁴) contrasts with Sst-IN→PC weakening. Proper identification of FS-INs (78.4% of EGFP+/tdTomato- cells) and morphological confirmation strengthen the findings.

result: FS-IN→PC synaptic transmission also increases during eye opening in the Cg1/2 area, with significantly larger uIPSC amplitude at P14-15 and P17-20 compared to P12-13.
evaluation: Claims C49-C50 extend the FS-IN→PC findings to prefrontal cortex, demonstrating that the strengthening is not restricted to visual cortex. This parallels the Sst-IN→PC findings in Cg1/2.

result: Synaptic transmission from Sst-INs to other interneurons (FS-INs and Htr3a-INs) does not change during eye opening, with stable connection probability and uIPSC amplitude from P12-13 to P14-15.
evaluation: Claims C51-C52 and C56-C58 demonstrate cell-type specificity of the eye opening effect. Statistical analyses (one-way ANOVA, p=0.767 for Sst-IN→FS-IN; p=0.907 for Sst-IN→Htr3a-IN) support the lack of change. This specificity is crucial for understanding the circuit reorganization.

result: Triple recordings demonstrate that at P12-13, Sst-INs produce similar uIPSCs in PCs and interneurons, but at P14-15, the same Sst-INs produce significantly larger uIPSCs in FS-INs and Htr3a-INs than in PCs.
evaluation: Claims C60-C63 provide direct evidence for target-specific changes using simultaneous recordings from the same presynaptic neuron. Paired t-tests (p=0.037 for both comparisons at P14-15) support the differential inhibition. This is strong evidence for postsynaptic mechanisms.

result: Dark rearing from P3 prevents the developmental weakening of Sst-IN→PC synaptic transmission, with no significant changes in connection probability or uIPSC amplitude between P12-13 and P14-15.
evaluation: Claims C64-C66 demonstrate that visual experience is necessary for the weakening. Statistical analyses (χ² test, p=0.066; unpaired t-test, p=0.702) support the lack of change. However, dark rearing eliminates both eye opening and pre-eye opening visual stimulation through closed eyelids.

result: Binocular lid suture from P8 prevents the weakening of Sst-IN→PC synaptic transmission in both visual cortex and Cg1/2, while artificial eye opening at P16 reproduces the weakening.
evaluation: Claims C67-C75 provide strong evidence that eye opening per se drives the changes. The artificial eye opening experiment (one-way ANOVA, p=0.008 for VC; p=0.003 for Cg1/2) is particularly compelling, demonstrating that the timing can be experimentally controlled.

result: Binocular lid suture prevents the strengthening of FS-IN→PC synaptic transmission, while artificial eye opening at P16 reproduces the strengthening in both visual cortex and Cg1/2.
evaluation: Claims C77-C82 demonstrate that eye opening also drives FS-IN→PC strengthening. Statistical analyses (one-way ANOVA, p=2.9×10⁻⁴ for VC) support the effect. This complements the Sst-IN→PC findings and demonstrates bidirectional regulation.

result: The weakening of Sst-IN→PC synaptic transmission is mediated by postsynaptic mechanisms, with significant decrease in quantal size (Q) from P12-13 to P14-15 but no changes in presynaptic release probability (PPR, C.V., failure rate) or number of release sites (N).
evaluation: Claims C84-C88 provide mechanistic insight through variance-mean analysis. The significant decrease in Q (Mann Whitney U test, p=2.9×10⁻⁴) with stable N (p=0.419) strongly supports postsynaptic mechanisms. The lack of changes in PPR, C.V., and failure rate rules out presynaptic contributions.

result: The strengthening of FS-IN→PC synaptic transmission is also mediated by postsynaptic mechanisms, with significant increase in quantal size (Q) from P12-13 to P14-15 but no changes in presynaptic parameters or number of release sites (N).
evaluation: Claims C89-C92 demonstrate that FS-IN→PC strengthening also involves postsynaptic mechanisms. The significant increase in Q (unpaired t-test, p=0.026) with stable N (p=0.439) parallels the Sst-IN→PC findings but in the opposite direction.

result: In Sst-tdTomato mice, ~5.2% of tdTomato+ neurons express PV and ~17.2% show FS properties with basket cell morphology, while non-FS tdTomato+ cells (95%) exhibit Martinotti cell morphology.
evaluation: Claims C26-C29 provide important characterization of the Sst-tdTomato line. The data show heterogeneity in the labeled population, with proper identification and exclusion of FS cells from Sst-IN analysis. This validates the experimental approach.

result: The kinetics of Sst-IN→PC uIPSCs show minimal changes during eye opening, with 10-90% rise time stable at P9-17 and half-width unchanged at P7-20. PC dendritic morphology also remains unchanged between P12-13 and P14-15.
evaluation: Claims C35-C38 demonstrate that the amplitude changes are not due to alterations in kinetics or dendritic filtering. The stable morphology (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) rules out space-clamp artifacts as an explanation for the amplitude reduction.

result: The developmental properties of Sst-IN→PC synaptic transmission are similar when using cesium-based high Cl- internal solution versus standard potassium-based solution.
evaluation: Claim C39 validates the recording conditions. The consistency across different internal solutions (Figure 1—figure supplement 4) strengthens confidence in the main findings and addresses potential concerns about driving force and space clamp.

result: Only ~1% of tdTomato+ Sst-INs express EGFP in Sst-tdTomato::Htr3a-EGFP mice, confirming that Sst-INs and Htr3a-INs are distinct populations.
evaluation: Claim C55 validates the genetic strategy for distinguishing interneuron subtypes. The minimal overlap confirms proper targeting and supports the interpretation of differential effects on different IN populations.

result: Eye opening occurs between P13 and P15, with 0% at P13, 77.9±7.4% at P14, and 100% at P15.
evaluation: Claims C124-C126 provide essential developmental timeline data. The precise timing (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) establishes the temporal correlation between eye opening and synaptic changes, though the 1-2 day window limits precise temporal resolution.

result: Eye opening differentially regulates inhibitory synaptic transmission in layer 2/3: weakening Sst-IN→PC transmission, strengthening FS-IN→PC transmission, leaving Sst-IN→interneuron transmission unchanged, with changes mediated by postsynaptic quantal size.
evaluation: Claims C93-C96 summarize the main findings. These summary claims are well-supported by the comprehensive experimental data presented throughout the manuscript, including developmental profiling, sensory manipulation, and mechanistic analysis.

result: Artificial eye opening can induce the weakening of Sst-IN→PC synaptic transmission, and this change is unlikely due to an intrinsic developmental program.
evaluation: Claims C71-C72 represent key interpretations supported by the lid suture experiments. The ability to prevent changes by suture and reproduce them by artificial opening strongly argues against an intrinsic developmental program, though complete exclusion of developmental factors is difficult.

result: Both connection probability and strength of Sst-IN→FS-IN and FS-IN→FS-IN synaptic transmission are comparable at P12-13 and P14-15 in continuously sutured mice.
evaluation: Claims C76 and C83 provide important controls showing that lid suture itself does not alter interneuron-to-interneuron connections. This specificity strengthens the interpretation that eye opening specifically affects interneuron-to-PC connections.

result: The average connection probability of Sst-IN→PC connections is ~58% within 100 µm at P12-20, consistent with previous reports in somatosensory cortex (~63%).
evaluation: Claim C99 validates the experimental approach by comparison with prior literature. The consistency with Xu et al., 2013 supports the reliability of the measurements, though discrepancies with other studies are noted in the discussion.

result: Prior work has established that sensory experience influences cortical development, eye opening drives rapid changes in the visual system, and excitatory connections strengthen after eye opening.
evaluation: Claims C8-C14 accurately summarize relevant prior work through appropriate citations. These establish the context for the current study, though the authors should be cautious about over-generalizing from cited work.

result: Prior work has characterized the properties and functions of Sst-INs and PV-INs in the neocortex, including their proportions, morphology, connectivity patterns, and roles in plasticity.
evaluation: Claims C15-C25 provide appropriate background on interneuron subtypes through citations. These establish the functional significance of the cell types studied and justify the focus on Sst-INs and FS-INs.

result: Htr3a-INs comprise ~50% of layer 2/3 INs, 5HT3a receptors are present exclusively in GABAergic INs, and Htr3a-INs encompass a heterogeneous population including Vip-INs and Npy-INs.
evaluation: Claims C53-C54 and C111 accurately cite prior characterization of Htr3a-INs. The acknowledgment of heterogeneity (C111) is important for interpreting the Sst-IN→Htr3a-IN results, as different subtypes may respond differently.

result: Prior work shows that GABAergic plasticity during the critical period has been studied, but changes during eye opening are less understood. Previous studies show layer- and region-specific differences in inhibitory development.
evaluation: Claims C97-C110 appropriately contextualize the current work within prior literature. The discussion of discrepancies between studies (layer differences, regional differences) is important for interpreting the current findings and highlights the novelty of the work.

result: GABAA receptors mediate inhibitory transmission, different subunits are selectively inserted at specific synapses, and subunit expression changes during development, potentially explaining the differential changes in Sst-IN→PC and FS-IN→PC transmission.
evaluation: Claims C112-C114 accurately cite established knowledge about GABAA receptors. However, C115 is speculative, proposing a mechanism without direct experimental evidence. While plausible, this hypothesis requires testing through receptor subunit analysis or pharmacological experiments.

result: The authors propose that decreased Sst-IN→PC inhibition after eye opening enhances visual input by facilitating dendritic events, while increased FS-IN→PC inhibition provides homeostatic rebalancing, potentially important for visual integration.
evaluation: Claims C116-C123 present a functional model based on the data and prior work. While the model is logical and consistent with known functions of these interneuron types, it remains speculative. Claims C118, C120, C122, and C123 are explicitly speculative and require in vivo functional validation.
